commenti.body:
I can answer that.

I’m pretty sure it’s for teenage girls to watch with their mothers. That’s the point of the movie.

I just watched it and I had pretty low expectations, but I thought they nailed it. Laughed my ass off. Perfect tone for a movie about a doll. Imho better than any “Lego” movie.

It ain’t the best movie of the year, but I feel like you have to try to not enjoy it.

tbh the fact that you felt the need to take this to TrueFilm says it all 

This movie was never intended to exist at this level of conversation. It’s supposed to be a movie for people who grew up with Barbie Dolls, whatever age they may be. It does an exceptional job at nailing exactly what it sets out to do. It does not try to impress snobby arthouse fans
You’re so wrong for throwing shade at the Lego movie, the Lego move and the Lego Batman movie are perfect

Agreed. I think movies should be mainly judged on if they accomplish what they're trying to do. Like Mission Impossible movies set out to be a thrill ride and most of the time they accomplish that. They may lack complex plots, stellar acting performances and intropspecrive social commentary but that doesn't automatically make them bad movies. Barbie absolutely accomplished what it set out to
What about the 2001 A Space Odyssey intro?  Who is that for?

> It does not try to impress snobby arthouse fans

No, Barbie is clearly trying to be something deeper.
It felt like it was directly for me

> to be honest, Im not sure who this movie is for

$1.5 billion at the box office and this dude is questioning whether there's an audience for it.

I’m not even a massive fan of it as a movie, but it’s inarguable that it did exactly what it was intended to do, and has become a clarion call for girls and women everywhere. Not every film needs to cater to what men think is cool or important. And I’d honestly rather cinemas full of movies like Barbie than another fucking Fast and the Furious or John Wick movie.

I don’t really like any of the lego movies, but I don’t hate on them or anything. I couldn’t really pay attention and I was watching them with children…maybe I missed something. But I didn’t think the humor was derived from character or plot beats and I thought that was a weakness. Whereas Barbie’s humor fit it like a glove (again, just how I felt)

you mean other than spoofing one of the most recognizable film intros of all time? 

There are significantly more obscure references than 2001 to the point that I’d even call harping that specific element of 2001 is mainstream
lol ironically yes. It’s sincere genuine filmmaking at its core trying to cut through pretension.
